issue.title: [LAG] LACP fallback feature not working as expected

failure.body:
Hi,

I am referring to [LACP fallback design document](https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/master/doc/lag/LACP%20Fallback%20Feature%20for%20SONiC_v0.5.md).

As per this,  `One and only one member port can be put into fallback mode per LAG`.

However, from implementation, is this handled?

From my testing, if a create LAG with fallback option, with 2 member ports, both the ports have enabled status when peer is not sending LACP PDU.
My expectation was that only one port will have status as enabled.

Could you please clarify on this.

resolution.title: [libteam] Support multiple ports with LACP fallback
resolution.description:
This brings #10823 up to date with current master branch.

#### Why I did it

Fixes #7555 and #8866.

While the LACP fallback HLD correctly describes the behavior for LAGs with multiple ports, the actual implementation only worked for single-port LAGs.

When multiple ports are present, the fallback mode would select all ports, therefore making it useless for the purpose described in the HLD (PXE-booting).

Therefore, this commit adds a patch to implement the desired behavior: If all non-disabled ports are defaulted, *one* port goes into fallback mode and gets selected for the LAG. As soon as any port receives a LACPDU, the fallback port goes back to defaulted. The fallback port is selected by higher port priority or, if both have equal priority (the default), by lower port number (as described in the HLD).
